assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, the active truncated peptide, pharmacological stability) turned into therapies that lower glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal events. Originality, clarity and exceptional clinical and societal impact make this the strongest case on the list.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1) and Drucker (receptor biology, tissue actions, DPP-4 and clinical translation) are the central academic contributors; Knudsen represents the pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues such as liraglutide and semaglutide. Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active peptide is contested in my recollection and the exact credit boundary is unresolved; Habener is not on this list.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large randomized outcome trials and global clinical use. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov versus others) is disputed and I have not verified it.
Whether the committee will recognise an industry scientist alongside academic discoverers.
Long-term safety and durability of effect of incretin therapies are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that TNF drives the cytokine cascade in rheumatoid synovium and that blocking it gives clinical benefit, validating cytokine-targeted therapy and opening a class of biologics used across rheumatoid arthritis, IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthropathies. A clear mechanism-to-patient discovery with lasting impact on autoimmune and inflammatory disease.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly led the synovial cytokine work and the first anti-TNF clinical trials, a clean two-person credit. Wider contributions (for example TNF cloning and antibody engineering by others) are not on this candidate list.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation and use of multiple agents. Recognition is timely and the field is stable, though some may consider the field's reception already well honoured by other awards.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the discovery as sufficiently fundamental versus translational.
Credit for the original TNF biology and antibody development by other investigators is outside this candidate's names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of SMN2 exon 7 splicing as a target and design of antisense oligonucleotides to correct it produced nusinersen, which transformed spinal muscular atrophy from a fatal infant disease into a treatable one. It also validated antisense splicing modulation as a therapeutic platform.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target discovery) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development) form a coherent pair. Other contributors, for example Ionis or academic SMA genetics groups, are outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong long-term clinical data and confirmation in other SMA therapies. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Relative weight of the SMN gene discovery (not on this candidate) versus the therapeutic invention.
Unclear whether the committee prefers discovery of platform principles to a single-disease drug.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors including costimulatory domains produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new category of living drugs. Major conceptual and clinical advance in cancer immunology.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation CD28 CAR design and preclinical work) and June (4-1BB CAR and the first durable clinical responses) are central; Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer work is foundational but the pair seems the most defensible allocation. Original CAR concept work by Eshhar is not on this list, which complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation, but long-term outcomes, toxicity and solid tumour efficacy remain open. Mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: Eshhar and other early CAR pioneers are not among the credited names, so the priority question is not fully resolvable here.
Rosenberg's role is not included in my proposal and could be argued either way.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancy and neurotoxicity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS, the second messenger cGAMP and STING explained how cells detect pathogen and self DNA and revealed a core pathway in antiviral defence, autoimmunity (interferonopathies, lupus-related mechanisms), and anti-tumour immunity. Highly relevant to my own field of autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Chen discovered cGAS and cGAMP as the DNA sensor and second messenger; Barber identified STING as the adaptor. Ishikawa co-identified STING and Sun and Wu contributed to the cGAS work, so a three-person limit forces difficult exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent replication and a rich mechanistic literature; clinical translation (STING agonists and antagonists) has so far been modest, which makes it somewhat early on the therapeutic side.
uncertainties: Several people share credit for STING identification.
Clinical validation of therapeutic targeting remains incomplete.
Possible interpretive overreach as the pathway is linked to many diseases.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsin and the optogenetic toolkit enabled causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and transformed experimental neuroscience, with extensions to cardiology and vision restoration. Methodological impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) characterised channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth and Boyden established neuronal use; Miesenböck's earlier work adds further complexity. With six credited names and a three-person limit, any allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Widely used for two decades and independently replicated; clinical applications are only beginning.
uncertainties: Severe attribution complexity across six names.
Whether the committee regards a tool as a discovery in the sense of the prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning of the T-cell receptor solved the central problem of how T cells recognise antigen and MHC and underpins modern immunology, from tolerance and autoimmunity to cancer immunotherapy. Foundational and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Mak's group and the Davis and Hedrick groups reported TCR chains independently in 1984; Yanagi also contributed. A three-person allocation leaves out one credited name.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of confirmation. The delay in recognition and priority disputes may argue against it now.
uncertainties: Priority dispute among the 1984 groups and whom to exclude.
Possible view that the discovery's moment for recognition has passed or that it is a foundation rather than a final discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, with population data showing sharp declines in disease. A major preventive-medicine achievement linking virology to cancer prevention.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLP assembly; Frazer, with Zhou, contributed to VLP production and the vaccine. Others (Kirnbauer, Zhou who died in 1999) complicate credit and cannot be recognised posthumously.
assessment.maturity: Strong effectiveness evidence, including population-level cervical cancer reductions. Timely, though zur Hausen already received the prize for HPV and cervical cancer.
uncertainties: Credit among the VLP groups is contested.
The earlier HPV prize may reduce the committee's appetite for further HPV-related recognition.
